lessons: Keep hooks concise and punchy; the video with the highest start retention (Tuna vs. Cod) used a strong visual and behavioral contrast immediately in its opening line.
Avoid starting with long, multi-clause scientific definitions or background facts (such as the maple syrup percentage drop), as viewers drop off steeply within the first 10-15% when over-explained.
Ensure the core mechanism or answer is introduced early; drops frequently occur around the 25% to 35% mark when the explanation of 'how it works' transitions too slowly.
Eliminate mid-video pauses or philosophical questions near the end (like the juice question in the spicy food video) which trigger a secondary wave of viewers to leave right before the finish.
Not enough data to determine the effect of countdowns since all entries had 'countdown: null'.
worst_moment_types: Dense background statistics and percentages delivered too early in the script
Slow transitions into the biochemical mechanism of the topic around the 25-35% mark
Extra rhetorical questions or tangents introduced late in the video near the final 10% of runtime
best_hook_types: Direct, high-contrast comparisons between two familiar things (e.g., Tuna vs. Cod meat)
Startling action-oriented statements about everyday foods or bodily reactions (e.g., pineapple eating you back)
Short, provocative premise statements that immediately challenge a common assumption
